data.long_meaning: The name Azarion is derived from the Hebrew word ‘azar’ which means ‘help’ or ‘aid.’ In the Bible, this name was given to a priest who served at the altar and helped the high priest in his duties (Zech 1:3). This name is a reminder of God’s help and support in our lives. The name Azarion carries the meaning “God has helped” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Azarion usually hope their child will grow to embody god has helped and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Azarion total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_hebrew.name: עזריאון
in_hebrew.meaning: אלוהים עזר לי (God has helped me)
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם עזריאון מורכב מהמילים 'עזר' ו'אלוהים' או 'יה', שפירושם 'אלוהים עזר לי' או 'עזר של אלוהים'. השם נמצא בשימוש בקרב יהודים וגם נוצרים, והוא מבטא את הרעיון של עזרה אלוהית.

in_greek.name: Αζαριών
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Αζαριών προέρχεται από τις Εβραϊκές λέξεις 'עזר' (βοήθεια) και 'אלוהים' (Θεός). Το όνομα αυτό χρησιμοποιήθηκε στην αρχαία Εκκλησία και αντανακλά την πίστη στην divine βοήθεια.

in_latin.name: Azarion
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Azarion derivatur ex verbis Hebraeis 'עזר' (adiutorium) et 'אלוהים' (Deus). Hoc nomen in usu est apud Christianos et exprimit notionem auxilii divini.

historical_references.reference: The martyrology of Adon, a 5th century Syriac text, records the martyrdom of a bishop named Azarion in the Persian Empire under Shapur II (310-379 AD). Azarion was a bishop from the city of Amid in Mesopotamia and was captured, tortured, and executed for refusing to abandon his Christian faith. His feast day is celebrated on May 27.
historical_references.context: Persian Empire, Martyrdom of Bishop Azarion

historical_references.reference: In the 6th century, the Byzantine historian Zonaras wrote in his 'Chronicle' about a bishop named Azarion who lived during the reign of Emperor Anastasius I (491-518 AD). According to Zonaras, Azarion was a bishop of Amida in Mesopotamia who was accused of heresy and exiled to a remote region. Azarion's followers maintained his innocence and eventually proved his orthodoxy, leading to his reinstatement as bishop.
historical_references.context: Byzantine Empire, Bishop Azarion's accusation of heresy
